ch7_lab_boxmodel.title: Quick Check: Box Model Math & Document Flow

questions.q: Using default content-box math, an element has width: 100px, 10px of padding, and a 5px border on every side. What is its total rendered width?

An

has margin-bottom: 30px and the

right below it has margin-top: 20px. Due to margin collapse, what is the actual visible gap between them?
options: 30px (the larger value wins, the smaller is absorbed)

questions.q: What is the key difference between display: none and visibility: hidden?
options: display: none completely removes the element from document flow so adjacent boxes fill the space; visibility: hidden hides it but still reserves its physical space
visibility: hidden removes the element from flow; display: none just hides it visually
display: none only works on images

questions.q: To turn a group of child elements into 'flex items,' which element do you apply display: flex; to?
options: You apply it to the CSS file itself, not any element

questions.q: In CSS Grid, what does the fr unit (e.g., grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr;) represent?
options: A fraction of the available free space in the grid container
A percentage of the viewport width

questions.q: What is the key difference between auto-fill and auto-fit when building a responsive grid?
options: auto-fill leaves empty ghost tracks if there's extra space; auto-fit collapses those empty tracks so existing items stretch to fill the row
auto-fit only works on Flexbox, not Grid
auto-fill requires media queries to work; auto-fit does not

ch7_lab_responsive.title: Quick Check: Positioning, Units & Media Queries

questions.q: How does position: sticky behave differently from position: fixed?
options: They are identical in every way
sticky acts like 'relative' until the user scrolls past a defined threshold, then it locks in place like 'fixed'; 'fixed' is glued to the viewport from the start
fixed scrolls normally with the page; sticky never moves at all

questions.q: Which relative unit is based on the font size of the root <html> element, not the direct parent?
Why does the chapter recommend a 'Mobile-First' strategy, writing base styles for phones and using min-width media queries to layer on desktop styles?
options: It forces you to prioritize essential content for users on the go, then progressively add complexity for larger screens
Mobile-First sites load slower on purpose
Desktop-First is actually faster and Mobile-First is outdated
